source.citation: 'New Things in Town. A Queer House Out on the Avenue. Reaper Man Glessner's Dutch House in the Aristocratic Precincts of Prairie Avenue.' Unidentified Chicago newspaper, undated (late 1887 by the museum's reading), a clipping pasted in the Glessners' scrapbook; transcribed by the Glessner House Museum, 'Queer, Quaint, and... Dutch??', The Story of a House (blog), 8 June 2015.
what_it_does_not_supply: the newspaper's name or the issue's date
what was actually planted, in 1887 or in 1904
a reading of the printed page
what_it_supplies: the court as the house's yard, enclosed from the street and the neighbours, about 40 by 100 ft by the reporter's figure
the plan in late 1887 to sod the court and set a fountain, flowers and shrubbery in it (an intention)
a stone porch at the house's angle over the court and a broad stair from the library and dining-room down to it
the stable at the rear, walled off from the house
a conservatory in the tower behind the roof, by the reporter's account
